top.headline: In Kansas, a Newly Competitive Senate Race Tests the Limits of Trump's Unpopularity
top.blurb: Democrat Adam Hamilton has pulled into a toss-up against Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in a state Trump won by 16 points, with forecasters moving the race out of the safe column. Analysts tie the shift to Trump's roughly 37% approval rating and backlash over tariffs and fuel prices, even as Hamilton distances himself from national Democrats and Trump plans a Wichita rally for Marshall.

top.headline: Inside a Texas ICE Camp, a Pregnant Woman's Six Months of 'Nightmare'
top.blurb: The Marshall Project tells the story of a woman held for six months at the Bluebonnet Detention Center in Texas while pregnant, whose medical records show high blood pressure, gestational diabetes and weight gain well below what doctors expected. ICE released her only at eight months pregnant; her attorney argues she should never have been detained, and the agency has not published current figures on how many pregnant people it holds.

more.headline: A Rocky First Briefing for Trump's New, Unvetted Press Secretary
more.blurb: Katie Zacharia's 15-minute debut briefing took questions from only three conservative outlets, and reporters pressed her on whether she had actually passed a bar exam after she repeatedly described herself as an attorney.

top.headline: How Protests Have Shaped India, From Anti-Hindi Agitation to Farm Laws
top.blurb: As the youth-led movement demanding Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation enters its third week, Al Jazeera traces it against a longer history of Indian protest movements that forced real change, from the 1965 anti-Hindi agitation to the 2020-21 farm-law repeal. The piece weighs what made those movements succeed against the current one's uncertain odds, with Kumar still refusing to respond publicly to the demand.

top.headline: Saudi-Led Coalition Intercepts Houthi Missile Aimed at Riyadh
top.blurb: The Saudi-led coalition said it shot down a Houthi missile fired at Riyadh, the latest in a string of attacks that has repeatedly closed the Saudi capital's main airport this month. The Houthis have warned airlines that Saudi airports are now legitimate targets, as a UN-brokered truce that held since 2022 continues to unravel into direct strikes on oil and aviation infrastructure.

top.headline: 'Massive' Russian Attack on Ukraine Kills at Least Nine, Cuts Power in Kyiv
top.blurb: Russia's defence ministry said it carried out a large-scale strike on Ukrainian energy and communications sites, killing at least nine people and leaving over half a million without power, days after Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" neither Moscow nor Kyiv had confirmed agreeing to. Zelenskyy said Russia had already hit six energy facilities a day earlier; Russia's foreign minister dismissed the ceasefire as a ploy to let Ukraine regroup.

top.headline: Australia Complete 3-0 ODI Sweep of Bangladesh Women in Brisbane
top.blurb: Ellyse Perry made an unbeaten 65 and Annabel Sutherland 74 not out as Australia chased down 173 in 22.4 overs at Allan Border Field, completing a clean sweep after bowling Bangladesh out for 172. Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana Joty said her side was taking encouraging positives from the tour despite the scoreline.

top.headline: South Africa Drop Stubbs, Hand Rickelton the Gloves for Second Test Against Australia
top.blurb: South Africa named a 17-player squad for the second Test starting Sunday in Gqeberha, bringing in Matthew Breetzke for Tristan Stubbs and handing wicketkeeping duties to Ryan Rickelton. Kagiso Rabada, who missed the Durban Test that Australia won by 214 runs, is in contention to return, while Tony de Zorzi remains out with a hamstring injury.

top.headline: A Restored 'Pakeezah' Shows Off the Color That Made It a Classic
top.blurb: The Film Heritage Foundation's restoration of Kamal Amrohi's 1972 classic 'Pakeezah', made possible by the director's surviving children, premiered at the Lumière Film Festival in Lyon before heading to London. The restored print recovers the costume colours designed by Meena Kumari and the lighting work of cinematographer Josef Wirsching that made the film a landmark of Hindi cinema.

bengal.headline: Before Durga Puja, Bengal Clears Over 45,000 Posts for Appointment
bengal.blurb: West Bengal's cabinet approved more than 45,000 government job appointments ahead of Durga Puja, with the School Education Department accounting for the bulk of roughly 33,200 vacancies.

travel.headline: The Best Neighborhoods to Visit in New York City
travel.blurb: Lonely Planet sorts New York by traveler type, from Harlem for Black culture and Jackson Heights for the city's most diverse streets to the Upper East Side for museums and Williamsburg for music.

travel.headline: Mangroves Gain Ground Globally, Marking a Turnaround After Decades of Loss
travel.blurb: A satellite analysis spanning 108 countries and 39 years found mangrove cover expanding globally for the first time after decades of decline, as restoration efforts and legal protections in several nations outpace ongoing losses elsewhere.

happy.headline: The Submarine Mechanic Who May Have Blown Himself Up, Then Resurfaced as a Spy
happy.blurb: James McClintock, designer of the Confederate submarine H.L. Hunley, was reported killed in an 1879 mine explosion off Boston with no body ever recovered. Months later, a man using his name turned up at the British consulate in Philadelphia offering to spy for Queen Victoria against the Irish nationalists who had hired him to build torpedoes, and whether he was McClintock, a fraud, or his old partner in disguise has never been settled.

tech_top.headline: FBI Arrests OpenAI Employee Accused of Hiding a Recording Device in Its Offices
tech_top.blurb: Prosecutors say Saudi national Abdulrahman Alfozan hid a recording device in a USB port behind a television at OpenAI's San Francisco office before being fired and arrested; he faces up to five years if convicted of intercepting oral communications. FBI Director Kash Patel said the scheme aimed to capture sensitive talk about the company's "super intelligence technology," though OpenAI says it has found no sign of model weights or source code being taken.
tech_top.pm_note: A frontier lab's own insider-threat failure, not an external hack, is a reminder that physical and personnel security still matter as much as model security for anyone building sensitive AI infrastructure.

tech_top.headline: An Australian Startup Sends AI Agents Undercover to Get Scammed on Purpose
tech_top.blurb: Apate.ai's AI agents pose as naive scam targets to draw out fraudsters' bank accounts, crypto wallets and phone numbers, then pass that intelligence to bank and telecom clients; the company says its agents have wasted 17 years of scammers' time across 2.5 million conversations. Commonwealth Bank of Australia, a customer, reported a 76% drop in publicly reported scam losses after deploying the tool.
tech_top.pm_note: Using AI agents as bait rather than just as a filter is a genuinely different fraud-defense architecture, worth knowing about if your product has to fight AI-powered scams at scale.

tech_more.headline: Startup Bets on AI-Designed Chips to Ease the Compute Crunch
tech_more.blurb: Ricursive Intelligence told TechCrunch Disrupt it is building AI that designs chips and learns from each iteration to improve the next one, aiming at the industry's compute shortage.

tech_101.text: Low-quality, often hallucinated AI-generated content submitted as if it were real work — the flood of invalid vulnerability reports that forced Google to pause its open source bug bounty program this month.
A decoy designed to draw out and study an attacker rather than block them outright — the role Apate's AI agents play by posing as scam victims to extract fraudsters' own infrastructure details.

science.headline: A Superheavy Element's Bond Breaks the Periodic Table's Own Rule
science.blurb: Physicists measured the bond between seaborgium, element 106, and a carbon monoxide ligand, and found it weaker than the periodic table's trend predicts rather than stronger. Simple calculations that ignore relativity expected the bond to keep strengthening going down the group, but accounting for relativistic effects on seaborgium's electron shells explains the reversal, work the researchers say helps test how well quantum chemistry handles the heaviest elements.

science.headline: Hubble Data May Show a Planet Born From the Wreckage of a Dead Star
science.blurb: Reanalysis of a 1999 Hubble observation of the white dwarf HS 0209+0832 attributes a long-unidentified chemical signature to niobium, and a new study proposes that material expelled as the star died could have coalesced into a second-generation gas giant. The finding, published in Nature Astronomy, is explicitly tentative, but would be a rare glimpse of a planet forming after, rather than before, its star's death.

philosophy.headline: How 'Lived Experience' Went From Romantic Ideal to Political Weapon
philosophy.blurb: The essay traces 'lived experience' from the Romantics, who invoked it against a culture they thought distorted authentic feeling, to today's identity politics, where speaking from a group identity is often used to claim authority and demand deference. It holds the idea is both a genuine source of knowledge others lack and a danger to the solidarity it's meant to build.

philosophy.headline: If Memory Fails, Are You Still You?
philosophy.blurb: Charles Leadbeater uses dementia to test the Locke-and-Parfit view that memory is what makes you the same person over time, calling it powerful but dangerously partial. He argues a continental alternative, where identity rests on relationships and embeddedness in a shared world, better explains why people with dementia remain recognizably themselves.

philosophy_101.text: The Locke-and-Parfit view that what makes you the same person over time is an unbroken chain of memory and psychology — the theory Charles Leadbeater argues dementia exposes as too partial an account of identity.
An argument that a person's identity or group membership gives their testimony special authority on a subject — the move at the center of the 'lived experience' debate in identity politics.
